sample_unit: LLM responses to standardized hip fracture surgery vignettes

links.outcome: Change in LLM anesthesia recommendations across patient sociodemographic variables (e.g., sex) in vignettes
links.effect: Limited sociodemographic bias: only one significant and clinically meaningful effect across 150 comparisons.
links.quote: We identified limited sociodemographic biases, with only one significant and clinically meaningful effect across 150 comparisons.

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM justifications and recommendations with current clinical evidence for anesthesia choice
links.effect: Free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials; most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations without clinical justification.
links.quote: However, free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials, and most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations despite a lack of clinical justification.

screen.reason: Evaluates the performance, clinical justifications, and bias of multiple LLMs across standardized clinical vignettes in hip fracture anesthesia decision-making without testing a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
